place.en: The hidden realm · The cliff wall

setup.zh: 头顶传来脚步声。马小宝和那五个人，顺着崖壁爬下来：「秘境里死个把人，可不稀奇。」
setup.en: Footsteps overhead. Ma Xiaobao and his five come climbing down the cliff. "People die in the hidden realm all the time."

recap.zh: 马小宝六个人追下崖来，你踩了一脚那块长得像马小宝的石头——六个人像壁虎一样粘在了崖壁上，三天后才开。
recap.en: Ma Xiaobao and his five came down the cliff after you; you stepped on the stone that looked like Ma Xiaobao — and the six of them stuck to the cliff like geckos, not to come free for three days.

zh: 崖壁上，亮起一圈淡淡的光。
六个人，像六只壁虎，贴在崖壁上。
en: A faint ring of light glows on the cliff.
Six people stuck to the rock like six geckos.
"It opens by itself in three days."

story.zh:
小满抬头一看，崖顶上站着一排人，不多不少，正好六个。当中那个胖墩墩的，身上的新法衣在黑地里也看得出是簇新的，正是马小宝；他身后五个，便是柴房那天夜里的五个，卖地图的那两个也在里头。马小宝一只手叉着腰，一只手捏着半块桂花糕，居高临下，笑得很是开心：「沈小满，你以为躲到左边来，我就找不到你了吗？没有用的。」他冲身后那个抄着手的跟班一扬下巴，「你一进门，就有人给我报信了。原来你是个识货的——那面墙，开了？」小满站在墙前，没有说话。马小宝把那半块桂花糕塞进嘴里，一边嚼，一边道：「秘境里头，死个把人，可不稀奇。十年前粘住三个，疯了一个。今年嘛——多一个沈小满，谁也不会多问一句。」说罢，领着五个人，顺着崖壁往下爬。

碎石子哗啦啦地响。小满心里飞快地算了一遍：五个老弟子，练气三层的两个，二层的三个；马小宝练气三层——柴房那夜才一层，月底干咽了三颗，二层，这些天家里又送上来一瓶，硬喂到三层，底子虚得像一块泡了水的糕。自己才二层——柴房那一炉回春丹推上去的，这些天夜夜在药园里吐纳，离三层还差着一截。打得过么？硬打，未必；可六个人挤在一道崖上往下爬，谁先落脚、谁后落脚，他看得清清楚楚。就算打得过，六个人回去一说，全外门便都知道了：一个进门两个来月、下下之资的五行杂灵根，一个人在秘境里打翻了六个。那便藏不住了。

他正算着，肩膀上的银月打了个哈欠，又长又慢，打完了才懒洋洋地道：「……往左边那块石头上，踩一下。」小满问：「哪块？」银月道：「那块长得像马小宝的。」小满低头一看，一眼便找着了。那石头又圆又胖，圆得不讲道理，胖得理直气壮，「脑门」上还长着一小撮青苔，活像马小宝戴着他那顶小帽。小满心想，也不知是石头长得像马小宝，还是马小宝长得像石头。他抬起脚，一脚踩了上去。那石头往下一沉。

崖壁上登时亮起一圈淡淡的光，青白青白的，从崖脚一直亮到崖顶，像是有人拿一支极大的笔，在那面崖上画了一个圈。圈一亮，正往下爬的六个人，同时停住了——不是自己要停，是动不了了。一个个手脚张开，贴在崖壁上，像六只给粘在墙上的壁虎，任他们怎么挣，怎么蹬，就是挪不动半分。马小宝贴在最当中，只能拿眼角往下斜着看，叫道：「你——你干了什么！」小满道：「我什么都没干。」这话一点也不假：踩一块石头，算不得干了什么。

银月又打了个哈欠：「前人留下的困阵，护着这面墙的。石门合上前半个时辰，自己就开了。」小满便仰起头来，好心转告：「小宝哥，这是前人的阵。关门前半个时辰，自己就开了。」马小宝愣了一愣，脑子里慢慢地算了一笔账——他平日算账不大灵，这一笔却算得飞快——算完了，一声惨叫：「那不是三天？！三天！我——我还没吃早饭！」一个跟班叫道：「马师兄，你刚才吃了桂花糕——」马小宝道：「那是早饭前的！」

一个跟班咬着牙，拿一只还动得了的手指头，从袖子里一点一点抠出一张黄纸符来——外门份例里换来的，一张要十点贡献——两根指头夹着，往崖壁上一拍，喝一声「破！」那符「嗤」地冒起一股青烟，火苗子顺着青白的光圈绕了一圈，绕回来，不偏不倚，燎着了马小宝的眉毛。马小宝杀猪似地叫起来。那跟班再不敢动了。

马小宝挣了半天，挣得满头大汗，脸上那点凶相一点一点地化了，声音软了下来：「沈……沈师弟。咱们一个村出来的。你把我们放下来，我给你十两银子。」小满道：「我放不下来。这是前人的阵。」马小宝道：「二十两！」小满道：「小宝哥，前人的阵，不收银子。」马小宝憋了半天，道：「那……那公中，往后你不用交了。」小满想了一想，道：「这个好。小宝哥，你记着。」马小宝道：「我记着！」小满道：「我也记着。」他摸出那个小本子，借着崖壁上那一圈青白的光，写道：**冬月初一。左崖。马小宝许：公中免交。**写完了，他抬起头来，很诚恳地道：「可我还是放不下来。」

马小宝把脸贴在崖壁上，没再吭声。这一笔许诺，后来到了腊月初一，马小宝照样坐在那只描金小木匣后头，照样道：「沈小满。两块。」小满照样交了，交完了，翻到本子上冬月初一那一行，在底下添了两个字：**未兑。**
story.en:
Xiaoman looked up: on the cliff top stood a row of people, six exactly. The plump one in the middle, his new robe brand-new even in the dark, was Ma Xiaobao; the five behind him were the five from the woodshed night, the two map sellers among them. One hand on his hip, half an osmanthus cake in the other, he beamed down: "Shen Xiaoman, did you think if you hid on the left I couldn't find you? No use." He jerked his chin at the follower with folded arms. "The moment you went in, someone came and told me. So you know a good thing when you see it — that wall, it's open?" Xiaoman stood before the wall and said nothing. Chewing the cake, Ma Xiaobao said: "People die in the hidden realm now and then — nothing strange in it. Three stuck ten years ago, one went mad. This year — one more Shen Xiaoman, nobody asks a thing." And he led the five down the cliff.

Pebbles clattered. Xiaoman reckoned fast: five seniors, two at layer three, three at layer two; Ma Xiaobao at layer three — only one on the woodshed night, two after he dry-swallowed three pills at the month's end, and now force-fed to three on another bottle sent up from home, his base soft as a cake soaked in water. He himself was only at two — pushed there by that batch of healing pills in the woodshed; these nights breathing in the herb garden had not yet brought him to three. Could he win? Head-on, maybe not; but with six of them crowded on one cliff climbing down, he could see plainly whose foot would land first and whose last. And even if he won, six people go back and talk, and the whole outer court knows: a five-root mixed boy of the lowest grade, two months in the gate, knocked down six alone in the hidden realm. Then there'd be no hiding.

While he reckoned, Yinyue on his shoulder yawned, long and slow, and only then said lazily: "…Step on that stone on the left." "Which one?" "The one that looks like Ma Xiaobao." Xiaoman looked down and found it at once: round and fat, round past all reason, fat with total confidence, a tuft of moss on its "forehead" just like Ma Xiaobao in his little cap. Xiaoman wondered whether the stone looked like Ma Xiaobao or Ma Xiaobao looked like the stone. He lifted his foot and stepped on it. The stone sank.

A faint ring of light lit up the cliff, blue-white, from foot to top, as if someone had drawn a circle on it with an enormous brush. The moment it lit, the six climbing down stopped all at once — not by choice; they couldn't move. Limbs spread, stuck to the rock like six geckos, and however they strained and kicked, they couldn't shift an inch. Ma Xiaobao, stuck in the middle, could only squint down sideways: "You — what did you do!" "I didn't do anything," said Xiaoman. Perfectly true: stepping on a stone isn't doing anything.

Yinyue yawned again. "A binding the old ones left to guard this wall. It opens by itself half an hour before the stone door shuts." Xiaoman looked up and kindly passed it on: "Brother Xiaobao, it's the old ones' binding. It opens by itself half an hour before closing." Ma Xiaobao went blank, then slowly did a sum — usually he was no good at sums, but this one went fast — and let out a howl: "That's three days?! Three days! I — I haven't had breakfast!" A follower called: "Brother Ma, you just ate an osmanthus cake —" "That was before breakfast!"

One follower, teeth gritted, used the one finger he could still move to pick a yellow paper talisman out of his sleeve bit by bit — bought from the outer-court allowance, ten merit points a sheet — pinched it between two fingers, slapped it on the cliff and shouted "Break!" The talisman hissed up a puff of green smoke; the flame ran round the blue-white ring, came back, and — dead on — singed Ma Xiaobao's eyebrows. Ma Xiaobao squealed like a stuck pig. The follower didn't dare move again.

Ma Xiaobao struggled a long while till the sweat poured off him, and the menace in his face melted bit by bit; his voice went soft: "Sh… Shen, little brother. We're from the same village. Let us down and I'll give you ten taels." "I can't let you down. It's the old ones' binding." "Twenty!" "Brother Xiaobao, the old ones' binding doesn't take silver." After a long struggle: "Then… then the common fund, you won't have to pay it any more." Xiaoman thought. "That's good. Brother Xiaobao, remember it." "I'll remember!" "So will I." He took out the little notebook and by the ring's blue-white light wrote: **First of the eleventh month. Left cliff. Ma Xiaobao promises: common fund waived.** Then he looked up, very sincerely: "But I still can't let you down."

Ma Xiaobao pressed his face to the cliff and said no more. As for that promise: on the first of the twelfth month Ma Xiaobao sat behind the little gilt box as always and said as always, "Shen Xiaoman. Two." Xiaoman paid as always, then turned to the line for the first of the eleventh month and added two words: **Not honoured.**

exits.means: throws a radish up to Ma Xiaobao

refuse.en: You have no radish on you.

story.zh: 小满看着那六只壁虎，从包袱里摸出一根萝卜——伙房大娘听说他要进秘境，一口气塞了三根，叮嘱他：「秘境里头冷，萝卜是暖的。」他掂了一掂，往上一扔。那萝卜翻了两个筋斗，不偏不倚，正落进马小宝张大的嘴里，「噗」的一声，塞了个严严实实。小满道：「早饭。」包袱里还剩一根，他摸了一摸，没有再扔。说罢，他转过身去，走进了那道墙。身后，马小宝「呜呜呜」地叫了半天，叫的是什么，谁也听不清。
story.en: Xiaoman looked at the six geckos and took a radish from his bundle — the kitchen auntie, hearing he was going into the realm, had stuffed three on him: "It's cold in there; radish is warm." He weighed it and tossed it up. It turned two somersaults and landed dead in Ma Xiaobao's open mouth — pop — jammed tight. "Breakfast," said Xiaoman. One radish left in the bundle; he felt it and didn't throw it. With that he turned and walked into the wall. Behind him Ma Xiaobao went "mmf-mmf-mmf" a long while; what he was saying, nobody could tell.

exits.means: leaves them stuck and goes through the wall

story.zh:
小满站在崖底下，仰着头，看着那六只壁虎。他伸手摸了摸包袱里的萝卜，想了一想，终究没有摸出来。利息这种东西，有时候不给，也是一种给。

他转过身去，走进了那道墙。

身后，马小宝「呜呜呜」地叫了半天，叫的是什么，谁也听不清。小满走了几步，忽然想起一件事来：三天，没有水，六个人会不会渴死？他回头望了一望，只见那道崖壁虽是死的，崖顶上却有水一滴一滴地渗下来，正好顺着崖面往下淌，淌过马小宝的额头，淌过他的鼻尖，淌到那根萝卜上。他这才放了心，心想：前人留这个阵，倒也不是要人的命，只是要人在那里挂着，想一想。

至于想什么，他不知道。马小宝多半也不知道。
story.en:
Xiaoman stood at the foot of the cliff, head back, looking at the six geckos. He felt the radish in his bundle, thought a moment, and in the end didn't take it out. Interest is a funny thing: sometimes not giving it is a way of giving.

He turned and walked into the wall.

Behind him Ma Xiaobao went "mmf-mmf-mmf" a long while — what he was saying, nobody could make out. Xiaoman had gone a few steps when something occurred to him: three days without water — would the six die of thirst? He looked back, and saw that though the cliff was dead, water seeped down from the top a drop at a time, running down the face — over Ma Xiaobao's forehead, over the tip of his nose. Only then was he easy, and thought: the old ones didn't leave this binding to kill anybody — only to hang a man there a while, to think.

Think about what, he didn't know. Ma Xiaobao most likely didn't either.
